newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says UK debt too high, must move to balance.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says UK debt too high, must move to balance.

text.p: Britain's public sector debt is still too high and must move towards balance, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said in an interview with the Evening Standard on Friday.
He added that there was no sign of overheating in Britain's housing market.
"We are still borrowing too much," Clarke said. "It is coming down but it has got to come down at the kind of pace that I think is necessary to get us towards balance."
Clarke also said British householders were enjoying a healthy, reviving housing market, with prices rising a little and prospects of sale improving.
"Not the slightest sign of overheating, bubble conditions, wild speculation, borrowers lending people too much money to buy houses they can't afford," Clarke said.
"None of the things that brought the big crash at the end of the Eighties."
